pointers.sentence: GDAL, the Geospatial Data Abstraction Library, reads and writes geographic data in many formats, vector data through its part called OGR, and transforms coordinates (`docs/ref/contrib/gis/gdal.txt`).

Neither is reached through a compiled extension: the documentation calls the GEOS wrapper "a BSD-licensed interface to the GEOS geometry routines, implemented purely in Python using ctypes", usable with no settings or database (`docs/ref/contrib/gis/geos.txt`).
GDAL is loaded when `django/contrib/gis/gdal/libgdal.py` is imported.

It loads the library as `lgdal`, and on Windows also as `lwingdal`, for some OSR routines a comment says are exported with the STDCALL convention, which `std_call` picks; then it sets `GDAL_VERSION` and installs `err_handler`, which logs each error GDAL reports to the logger "django.contrib.gis" (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/libgdal.py`).

`load_geos` finds GEOS the same way, from `GEOS_LIBRARY_PATH` or the names "geos_c" and "libgeos_c-1" on Windows, "geos_c" and "GEOS" on POSIX, but raises `ImportError` when it cannot (`django/contrib/gis/geos/libgeos.py:load_geos`).

Importing `django.contrib.gis.geos` asks at once: in a run that wrapped ctypes's loader, it loaded GDAL, which `django/contrib/gis/geos/geometry.py` imports, then GEOS, from the class body of `WKBWriter`, which keeps the library's version as a class attribute (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:WKBWriter`).

`GEOSGeometryBase.contains` passes the two geometries' pointers to `geos_contains` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/geometry.py:GEOSGeometryBase.contains`).

That is a `BinaryPredicate`, a kind of `GEOSFuncFactory`, which holds what the prototype needs: the C function's name, "GEOSContains", two geometry pointers as argument types, a byte as result and `check_predicate` as check (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/predicates.py:BinaryPredicate`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/predicates.py:UnaryPredicate`).

At its first call it makes the prototype and keeps it in `GEOSFuncFactory.func` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/libgeos.py:GEOSFuncFactory`).

The handle, a `GEOSContextHandle`, is made at a thread's first call and kept in a thread-local object; it starts a context with GEOS_init_r, sets the context's notice and error handlers, and ends it with GEOS_finish_r when collected (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/threadsafe.py:GEOSFunc.__call__`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/threadsafe.py:GEOSContextHandle`).

`check_predicate` turns 1 and 0 into `True` and `False` and raises `GEOSException` for anything else (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/errcheck.py:check_predicate`).

Its prototypes are made at import, by functions that set the types and the check on the library's own function objects (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/prototypes/generation.py`), and an OGR error code becomes `GDALException`, or `SRSException` for an unsupported coordinate system (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/error.py:check_err`).

`CPointerBase.ptr` hands out the pointer kept in `CPointerBase._ptr`, but raises rather than give C a NULL pointer: `GEOSException` on the GEOS side, `GDALException` on the GDAL side (`django/contrib/gis/geos/base.py:GEOSBase`, `django/contrib/gis/gdal/base.py:GDALBase`).

When the object is collected, `CPointerBase.__del__` passes the pointer to `CPointerBase.destructor`, GEOSGeom_destroy for a GEOS geometry (`django/contrib/gis/ptr.py:CPointerBase`).

An object whose C object depends on another keeps the other's wrapper alive: a `Layer`, which has no destructor, holds its `DataSource` (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/layer.py:Layer.__init__`), a `Feature` its layer, and a `PreparedGeometry` its geometry, for the crash of ticket #21662 (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prepared.py:PreparedGeometry.__init__`).

A ring read from a polygon or a member from a collection is a clone, and so is a copy of a geometry, since a copy sharing the pointer "may contain an invalid pointer location if the original is garbage collected" (`django/contrib/gis/geos/geometry.py:GEOSGeometryBase.__copy__`).

`GEOSGeometry` is made from a string of WKT, EWKT, HEXEWKB or GeoJSON, a memoryview of WKB, a pointer, or another geometry, which it clones (`django/contrib/gis/geos/geometry.py:GEOSGeometry.__init__`).
A string is matched against regular expressions first, which a comment says keeps malicious input from the C library (`django/contrib/gis/geometry.py`).

A reader first counts the geometry collections, nested in WKT and in all in WKB, and refuses more than `MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS`, 198, unless `max_geom_collections=` says otherwise; the release notes of 6.0.8 give the reason, a crash in GEOS (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKTReader.limit`, `docs/releases/6.0.8.txt`).

`==` asks for equal SRIDs and exact equality, coordinate for coordinate (`django/contrib/gis/geos/geometry.py:GEOSGeometryBase.__eq__`); `GEOSGeometryBase.equals` is the topological test.

`GEOSGeometryBase.transform` goes through GDAL: an `OGRGeometry` made from the WKB is transformed and read back as WKB, in place or, with `clone=True`, as a new geometry (`django/contrib/gis/geos/geometry.py:GEOSGeometryBase.transform`).

Points, lines and polygons can also be made from coordinates, collections from geometries, and all behave as lists, a point of its coordinates, a polygon of its rings, a collection of its members, through `ListMixin` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/mutable_list.py:ListMixin`).

Setting one item of a point or a line changes its coordinates in place; a point or a line whose length changes, and a polygon or a collection on any change to its list, builds a new GEOS geometry from the new list, takes its pointer, keeps the SRID and destroys the old (`django/contrib/gis/geos/linestring.py:LineString._set_single`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/polygon.py:Polygon._set_list`).

`OGRGeometry` is GDAL's geometry; a geometry crosses between the libraries as WKB, by `GEOSGeometryBase.ogr` one way and `OGRGeometry.geos` the other (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/geometries.py:OGRGeometry`).

A `SpatialReference` is a coordinate system, from an EPSG code, WKT, a PROJ string or a name such as "WGS84", and a `CoordTransform` a transformation between two (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/srs.py:SpatialReference.__init__`).

`DataSource` opens a file of vector data in any format GDAL reads, a `Layer` gives its features, and a `Feature` its geometry and fields, each an instance of the class for its OGR type (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/datasource.py:DataSource`, `django/contrib/gis/gdal/field.py`); `LayerMapping` loads models from them ([GeoDjango's forms, admin, feeds and data tools](gis-extras.md)).

A `GDALRaster` is opened from a path, made from a file's bytes, which it writes into GDAL's in-memory file system and removes when collected, or made new from a dictionary, in memory by default (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.__init__`).
